text: The harness drives the screens through the gateway-bff composite routes (DP-19) and calls each owning service only on its own base /api/recovery/<short>/v1 (DP-13); the SIT identity set named as DL40 in the legacy story remains the source of test users, and its group names are configuration.
why: DL40 is not in this run's source set and the microservice target adds the gateway hop; the load, the user count and the pass criteria are fixed by the legacy story and are not changed.
read: RWB-TE-009 sections 3, 4 and 12; Arch v5 slide 20 (gateway-bff) and slide 48 (414 concurrent staff at peak); DP-13; DP-19
confirm: QA lead and platform edge owner at the harness configuration review
impact: The route list, the identity groups and the stage name are configuration; the 410-user load, the 2,000 ms p95 limit and the 1 percent error limit are unchanged.

text: The 2,000 ms 95th-percentile target is measured at the gateway-bff response for each screen request, so the one-hop composite call of the gateway sits inside the measured budget; no per-service budget is added or subtracted.
why: The legacy story measures the screen request (NFR-008) on the monolith base; in the target the screen request is served by gateway-bff, so the measurement point has to be named.
read: RWB-TE-009 section 2 and section 8 rule BR2; Arch v5 slide 20 (gateway-bff, 2 s timeout, composite calls in parallel); DP-19
impact: A per-service measurement would read lower than the legacy limit and would not prove the screen target the user feels.

text: Screen labels in Thai and English are read from the reference-data contract of rwb-case (P3, DP-07) and role codes from the rwb-access contract (P4); the six screens are opened through the gateway-bff composite routes (DP-19).
why: The legacy story reads label_en and label_th from lov_value and role_code from role; the target moves reference data to rwb-case under the default ruling and puts every staff screen behind gateway-bff.
read: RWB-TE-010 section 11 and section 12; Template and Rules section R3 default ruling (reference data to P3); ownership map lov_value and reference_row owner P3; DP-07; DP-19
impact: Label and role checks read through published contracts; the runner keeps no local copy of reference data.

text: The scan engine's WCAG 2.1 A and AA rule tags, the four browser configurations (current and previous major versions of Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome) and the pipeline stage name are configuration in the scan profile, browsers.json and the pipeline file, because none of the three is named in the source documents.
why: The legacy story fixes the standard and the browser policy but not the engine or the stage name; the values must stay configuration so a browser or engine change needs no code change.
read: RWB-TE-010 sections 3, 4 and 8 rules BR2 and BR5; DL37 is not in this run's source set
confirm: QA lead and TechX code owner
impact: No business value in code; a missing browser stays a failure, never a skip.
